A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FiPS and retain matching methods and vision experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the added LLM material.

before.justification: v2 reports original FiPS compression and transfer-learning accuracies, ablations, and latency and memory measurements, alongside attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v3 retains original vision experiments and adds WikiText-2 perplexity results for four Gemma-2 and Llama-3 model variants in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain shared SVD initialization, dense bases and sparse factors, block-wise reconstruction loss, GMP, and optional RigL fine-tuning. The LLM application introduces no documented algorithmic component. Neuron-growth procedures are retained in Appendix A.1.2.

E1.justification: v3 adds autoregressive language-model compression, using SlimPajama for calibration and WikiText-2 for evaluation. This substantially extends the previous vision-only coverage. ImageNet-1k and the four image-classification transfer datasets remain.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates an individual-FC truncated-SVD baseline with block-wise error minimization against FiPS for Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.2-3B. The existing AAFM/GFM and vision sparsification comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The reported vision calibration set changes from 3,840 to 2,560 images. New LLM protocols use 163,840 calibration tokens, 40 epochs, and perplexity evaluation with a 2,048-token context. Sensitivity-analysis budgets and calibration grids also change. The unchanged main vision scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sparsity and calibration/training-length analyses are revised in v3 Figures 4b–c, corresponding to v2 Figures 6b–c. Appendix Table 7 extends structured-sparsity analysis to a 75% parameter budget. Component, sharing-group, density-correlation and neuron-growth analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions present point estimates without disclosed repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The reported Pearson-correlation analysis also remains unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 3 adds LLM perplexities, including FiPS 7.47 versus SVD 41.03 for Gemma-2-2B at a 50% MLP budget. Sparsity/calibration plots contain replacement results under revised settings, and Appendix Table 7 adds structured-sparsity scores at a 75% budget. Tables 1–2 retain their numerical entries.

T1.justification: The shared-basis construction, concatenation equations, excess-MSE expression and reconstruction objective remain mathematically equivalent. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the central contribution from vision-transformer compression to both ViTs and LLMs. v3 newly claims 40–50% reductions in Gemma-2 and Llama-3 MLP parameters with negligible perplexity degradation, substantially broadening claimed applicability.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds arguments about generalization to unseen text and compressed LLMs serving as alternatives to smaller models. Calibration selection is reframed as an accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. v2's explicit dedicated-kernel limitation and preliminary qualification of latency benchmarks are removed.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a FiPS source-code reference, exact checkpoint links, and LLM block groupings, learning rates, hardware and calibration times. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v2's explanation of divisible-by-64 tensor shapes and 16-bit requirements for latency benchmarking is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds an LLM-related-work paragraph and references covering Gemma, Llama, text datasets and calibration-data selection. The existing positioning relative to pruning, tensor decomposition and parameter-sharing methods is largely preserved.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting affects the abstract, introduction and explanatory sections. Main results are divided into vision and language subsections, appendices are reorganized, and neuron-growth and profiling material are moved. An impact statement is added; Section 5 also acquires a duplicated sparsity-distribution paragraph.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, with widespread figure resizing, recoloring and caption revisions. The method diagram and profiling figure move to the appendices. Vision tables receive compact main-text presentations and fuller appendix displays, and an LLM results table is added.

improvement.justification: The LLM evaluations provide useful evidence for applicability beyond vision, while code/checkpoint references and additional experimental details improve reproducibility documentation. These constitute a limited net gain. The broader quality-retention claims are insufficiently qualified: Table 3 shows Llama-3.2-3B perplexity increasing from 6.19 to 9.70 at a 50% MLP budget despite claims of negligible degradation. Removed benchmarking caveats also temper the improvement.
